govdocs-archive_org-StThomasAquinasTheCa: St. Thomas Aquinas’s Catechetical Instructions give his teachings on the Creed, the sacraments, and the Lord’s Prayer. The Angelic Doctor’s plain Lenten sermons instructed the faithful of Naples. Their clarity is unmatched. The book is a gem of medieval catechesis.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-HostyJamesPJrSA: Tom Johnson’s Note to FBI Destroyed; Kennedy Not Named is a Dallas Times Herald piece. The destroyed note was a scandal. The note was Oswald’s. The file belongs to the press archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-JenkinsMarionTh: This item — M. T. Jenkins, M.D., creator unknown — is an archive file. The file’s full context is unclear. Its subject seems to be the JFK case. Archivists value such fragments. The item is a fragment of the archive.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-LeyvaRogelioHer: This FBI report on Rogelio Hernandez Leyva — charged with air piracy — is a Bureau file. The declassified report is a primary source. Air piracy plagued the 1960s. The report may hold a clue. The file belongs to the government archive.
on-the-trail-of-pontiac-or-the-pioneer-b: Edward Stratemeyer's pioneer adventure follows brave boys on the Ohio frontier in the days of the great chief Pontiac. Forest trails, Indian councils, and settler cabins fill a story of courage in the wilderness. Written for young readers hungry for frontier excitement, it delivers history-flavored adventure at full gallop.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-and-dio: This 1913 Catholic reference piece on Bobbio — St. Columbanus' house in Italy, later a bishop's see — tells its long tale. Reginald Walsh covers its famed book room too. Columbanus' monks copied old books by candlelight there. Irish monks brought books and bells to Lombard Italy.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ajaccio: A 1913 entry on Ajaccio — the Corsican diocese of Napoleon's birthplace. Georges Goyau tells its island story. The emperor was baptized in its cathedral. Faith endures on the rugged isle. Corsica's church, through stormy times. Its bishop blessed the young Bonaparte.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alessio: A 1913 entry on Alessio — Lezhë, the Albanian diocese of Skanderbeg's league. Elisabeth Christitch gives its story. The national hero died within its walls. Faith survived the Ottoman centuries. A see of heroic memory. Its castle watched the Drin valley. Its lagoon mirrors the mountains.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alexis-franco: A 1913 entry on Alexis-François Rio — the French historian of Christian art. Beda Kleinschmidt honors his pioneering work. His Art chrétien opened new eyes. He found beauty in the Middle Ages. A prophet of Gothic revival. His taste shaped the Gothic revival.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ancient-see-o: This 1913 reference piece on the ancient see of Växjö — the Småland bishopric. Arthur Taylor gives its story. St. Sigfrid baptized its forests. The old see fell to the reformers. A vanished bishopric of Sweden. Its forests hid the first Christians.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-andrea-del-ve: A 1913 entry on Andrea del Verrocchio — the master of Leonardo. Gaston Sortais honors his workshop. His David and Colleoni stand immortal. Goldsmith, painter, and sculptor in one. Florence's great teacher. His bronze boy charms the Bargello. His tomb lies in Florence's soil.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-andrea-pallad: This 1913 reference piece on Andrea Palladio — the architect of the Veneto. Ralph Adams Cram honors his villas and churches. His Four Books taught the world. The Redentore crowns the Venetian shore. The master of the classical revival. His style built a thousand mansions.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-antonio-bosio: A 1913 entry on Antonio Bosio — the Columbus of the catacombs. Maurice Hassett honors his Roma sotterranea. His maps opened the underground city. The martyrs' graves owe him their fame. The father of Christian archaeology. His engravings guide the modern digger.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-arnolfo-di-ca: A 1913 entry on Arnolfo di Cambio — the architect of Florence's cathedral. Thomas Poole honors his mighty design. His campanile plan shaped the city. The Duomo rose from his drawings. The master builder of Florence. His tabernacle graces old St. Peter's.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-bartholomew-o: A 1913 entry on Bartholomew of San Concordio — the Dominican canonist. John Volz honors his Summa de casibus. His handbook guided the confessors. The schools prized its clear order. A friar among the moralists. His Pisanella was the confessors' vade mecum.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-benedict-of-s: A 1913 entry on Benedict the Moor — the Sicilian Franciscan saint. Johann Peter Kirsch honors his humble holiness. The lay brother's wisdom drew all. Palermo keeps his shrine. The black saint of Sicily. His kitchen was his oratory.
